answer: Optical physical unclonable functions resist Sybil attacks by binding agents to physical hardware. A verifier shines a violet laser through a disordered microstructure, recording how speckle patterns ripple across a sensor. Because each token is a physical relic of fabrication, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of manufacturing discrete optical hardware per identity. However, adversaries observing sufficient challenge-response pairs can train neural surrogates to spoof responses digitally.
